faqs.a: It checks whether text follows the JSON grammar exactly. Beyond parse success or failure, it also scans for duplicate keys, trailing commas, comments, and byte-order marks, and reports document statistics.
faqs.q: What does the JSON Validator check?

faqs.a: Yes - technically the last value wins and parsers accept it. But it is almost always a copy-paste bug, and it makes documents confusing. The validator flags every repeat with its path and line.
faqs.q: Are duplicate keys actually a problem?

faqs.a: No. Despite being common in config files (JSONC), comments are not part of the JSON specification and strict parsers reject them. The validator flags them explicitly.
No. Trailing commas are a JavaScript convenience, not valid JSON. Every strict parser rejects them. Remove the comma before the closing bracket or brace.
faqs.q: Is a trailing comma valid JSON?

faqs.a: The tool reports the character position from the parser and converts it to line and column. The most common causes: missing quotes, trailing commas, single quotes, and unquoted keys.
faqs.q: How do I find the exact error location?

faqs.a: A BOM (byte-order mark) is an invisible character some editors add at the start of a file. It breaks strict JSON parsers, so the validator flags it when present.

json-validator.formula:
strict parse:  JSON.parse(text)  -> ok, or error with position -> line/column
duplicate keys: scan raw text, track each object's key set -> repeats listed
trailing comma:  , followed by } or ]  (outside strings)
comments:  // or /* */ outside strings  -> flagged
BOM:  first char U+FEFF  -> flagged
All scans are string-aware: braces inside "..." are ignored.

keyFacts: JSON Validator checks strict JSON syntax plus four common problem patterns.
Duplicate object keys are flagged with their JSONPath and line number - parsers silently keep the last value.
Trailing commas and comments (JSONC habits) are detected, not just rejected.
A byte-order mark (BOM) at the start of the file is flagged because it breaks strict parsers.
Errors report the parser's character position converted to line and column.
Document statistics show bytes, total keys, nesting depth, and top-level type.

limitations: Only strict JSON is accepted: the checks explain rejections but cannot fix non-standard input.
Duplicate detection is textual: keys that differ only by Unicode normalization may be missed.
Number precision follows JavaScript doubles; very long numbers may lose precision when parsed.
Extremely large documents may be slow since all scans run on the main thread.

json-validator.workedExample:
Invalid sample:
{
  // user record
  "name": "Asha",
  "name": "Asha Sharma",
  "age": 30,
}

Result: Invalid JSON. Checks report:
- Strict parse: Fail - the parser rejects the // comment on line 2 (the exact message is shown live).
- Duplicate keys: Fail - Duplicate key "name" at $ (line 4).
- Trailing commas: Fail - comma before the closing brace on line 5.
- Comments: Fail - // comment on line 2.
- BOM: Pass.

Fix all four, and the document validates cleanly.
